searchText: You are also not a multi-chain wallet provider. 😉 I suspect multi-chain wallet providers care a whole lot more about cross-chain solutions than Ethereum core devs and EF people care about cross-chain compatability. Yep, that’s fair! Doesn’t change my opinion though: if Celo calls its 1559 implementation something different, then odds are that’s not the only custom bit of work you need to do to integrate Celo. And, similarly, if a network _is_ that easy to integrate., I suspect they have likely forked geth and this approach should work for them too It won't even work for ETH2, which has this type of transaction natively. We could call it "EIP-1559", but that would be a misnomer in that environment since they *started* with it. ETH2 only picks up 1559 transactions *from* EIP1559. Currently it has no transactions at all and when it does it will be because it inherited the current PoW chain. Well, I guess another way to phrase it would be that ETH2 will have the concept of a base fee and whatnot even if EIP-1559 fails, or changes, or whatever. It is likely that 1559 will go into ETH1 and then the transaction format will be the same or similar come ETH2, but that isn't a hard requirement. But if 1559 doesn't go into Eth1 then when the merge happens Eth2 will just inherit the non-1559 transactions from Eth1. There's no change to Eth1 transactions proposed for the merge as it's aiming to be as minimal as possible. Basically Eth2 is just a continuation of Eth1 so if it makes sense in Eth1 it also makes sense in Eth2 unless its specifically about PoW consensus. For the quick merge, yes. However, my understanding is that once the beacon chain (or its spiritual successor) takes over transaction processing it will/would have supported base fee style regardless of whether 1559 went in previously or not. Of course "what is The Merge" has gone through a lot of iteration recently so that statement may no longer make sense. 😄 1559 style mechanics were always planned for the future of Ethereum and eth2 is the future of Ethereum so yeah it was expected to have it. But if 1559 failed on eth1 then my guess is that would have to be reconsidered. But I think the overriding principle has been that eth2 is a continuation of eth1. This above conversation is why I think any capabilities system should be as concrete as possible. My understanding is <@!135612611923279872> is specifically looking for a way to know if a certain chain at a certain fork supports the `0x2` transaction type on `eth_sendRawTransaction`. If that's the issue, one option instead of querying the provider would be to maintain a computer-readable document somewhere (say github) that enumerates what transaction types become available at what block number per chainId. The plus side of this approach is it doesn't really require the clients to agree on a query format, the downside is it's maintained "out of tree" so can become stale. Where is the call? cc <@543900561460822016> https://consensysmesh.zoom.us/j/96923822358?pwd=bmVod1dJRUZiUE0za09RTWNLNmFxUT09 Doesn't appear to be in the lounge this time. 😛 per https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/283 Yeah, I feel like this is easy for clients to support via an endpoint, and to update as things change. If legacy txns get dropped post-merge, then whatever that endpoint returns would have to be updated. I don't see what the big problem with that is 🤔 ? Requires centralized curation, instead of fully decentralized endpoint-specified configuration. If we prepare for a world with any number of chains with any number of features, including test and development networks, then no central repository makes sense to try to maintain. Yeah, so I guess there needs to be a mapping of chainId => supported txn types _somewhere_, and the question is where? That mapping implicitly happens for mainnet + testnets by looking at the EIPs, but it isn't great Yes, and as a wallet that wants to be evm-chain agnostic, I want to be able to trust a chain itself, not "yet another centrally maintained github registry".
